utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Osmanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Today we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis, with Judge Morrison being away due to his urgent personal matters. Mr. Karadzic, are you ready to start your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency. Good morning, Excellencies. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Osmanovic.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, allow me to express my sympathy and compassion with regard to your losses, particularly that of your sister, whose conduct did not contribute in any way of her deserving to meet the fate that she did, and please believe me, I am telling you this from my heart. With your consent, I would now endeavour to clarify as precisely as possible all your statements so that we ultimately arrive at the exact truth. You have testified in at least four cases and gave at least four statements; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Basically, at the beginning of your each of your statements you describe the attendance and the religious congregation at Han Pijesak, and you criticised the flying of the Serbian flag and the singing of the Serbian song. Mr. Osmanovic, do you know that the Serbian Orthodox Church, even during the Turkish rule, had its own banner, and that was a different one from the state standard?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that the Serbian Orthodox Church had its banner. I didn't criticise the fact that they were flying the banner and singing the songs. Those were Chetnik songs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that they had a banner, but you also said that they sang nationalist songs that had been prohibited. Can you tell us which songs you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "From Topola to Ravna Gora."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "All the Guards Belong to General Draza"?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are Topola and Ravna Gora in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Western Allies never considered General Draza and Chetniks their foes, that General Draza was accorded a medal by the US president and that, quite recently, Draza Mihajlovic and his movement have been rehabilitated by a court?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the speakers please pause between questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Osmanovic, you are being requested by the interpreters to put a pause between the question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that you don't know that he was rehabilitated, but do you know that the Western Allies never considered Draza Mihajlovic their enemy?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the Western allies, Mr. Karadzic, but I know that the Communist Party of Yugoslavia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, where are we going? Let's come to the issues of the case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Your Excellency, I think that the point of departure of this witness is very important, and I want to find out what he thinks that is inadmissible when it comes to Serbs, whether it's the Chetnik Movement or whatever, and that was the first movement of that kind in the Balkans. So there was no mention of Muslims or anyone else. So if his basic position is anti-Serb, then it explains some other things as well. Very well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, you are said to be an anti-Serb. Would you like to comment on that, Mr. Osmanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, I would like to comment on it that. I have nothing against the Serbs. My family is of mixed ethnicity. My uncle and my brother were married to Serb women. Thirty per cent of my family used to live and work with the Serbs. I had Serb neighbours. We visited each other on religious holidays. We attended baptism ceremonies, et cetera, on sad and on joyous occasions equally. In this song, Nikola Kalabic was mentioned and he was a Chetnik leader during the Second World War who was convicted by the Communist authorities for his crimes committed against the Muslims and part of the Serbian nation, and for that reason, I said that I didn't approve of those songs. As for the Serbs themselves, I personally have nothing against them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us move, then, directly to Vlasenica and the issues relating to it. You said that in April you noticed that there were divisions and tensions between the Muslims and the Serbs. Do you agree that before April a war had started and ended in Croatia in which volunteers from Vlasenica, Muslim volunteers, took part in fighting the Serbs and that Muslims from Vlasenica used to go to Croatia to undergo secret training for police work, that they were sent there by the SDA?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: There's at least three questions in that, maybe more, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Remember the invaluable advice from Judge Baird. Make -- put your question in a simpler form.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: First question: Do you know that up until April 1992, the Croatian war started and ended?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it began, but I don't know that it ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. There was some sort of Vance-Owen Plan that appeased this battle-field, but do you know that Vlasenica Muslims used to go to Croatia to fight as volunteers with the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the SDA used to send its members, its trusted members, along the party line to attend training courses for policemen in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that before April of that year, the political life in Bosnia-Herzegovina was very tumultuous and that all this had to do with intentions of the Muslim party to secede from Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was a referendum on the secession.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it also very exciting in the Assembly and on the government? Was the whole previous year imbued by very tense political atmosphere?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw these political tensions in the Assembly of BH on TV in which you, esteemed sir, took part in. You were one who contributed to those tensions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in Vlasenica agreements had been concluded on forming two or maybe three separate municipalities out of one Vlasenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that a Serbian municipality of Vlasenica was established with a seat in Milici. I don't know what's the third one that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Milici separated separately and the rest of Vlasenica should have become the basis for constituting two separate municipalities and that each village was designated to which of those individual municipalities it would belong?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that this agreement was publicly acclaimed by opposition parties and that that was even publicised in early April?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we briefly look at 1D4127 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Emir Rabija is a Muslim name?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let me see the paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. We'll get back to this later. It seems that it hasn't been uploaded in e-court yet. Did you know that parallel with the negotiations on forming two municipalities and two police stations and all the other issues apart from the town infrastructure, the SDA [Realtime transcript read in error "NCA"] was involved in preparations for a war?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the SDA was arming the Muslims and that the Patriotic League in every municipality in April already had their staffs and units?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that it existed in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. Just at line 14 of page 6, as interpreted, the question reads something like: "... apart from the town infrastructure, the NCA was involved in preparations for the war," and I'm sure there wasn't an intention to use the words "NCA."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Perhaps SDA.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, the interpreter said "SDA."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that before that critical 21st or 23rd of April, a large number of both Serbs and Muslims were leaving Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that Milenko Stanic, the municipality president and Mr. Izet Redzic, the chairman of the Executive Council, went to a rally in Tuzla in which they invited the refugees to come back?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether these two gentlemen went to Tuzla, but I know that those people who returned from Tuzla after the capture of Vlasenica never left Vlasenica again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So do you know that the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, on the 12th of April, issued an order and directive to attack the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you must have known that, because that was published the next day, because we received that from well-intentioned Muslims, and we made it public the very next day.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that after that, until the 17th or the 18th of April, Redzic and all the other SDA deputies had left, including the leadership of the SDA and other Muslim officials, that they all left Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when they left or where they left, but I know that, unfortunately, I and my family stayed behind, including a large number of my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I feel complete solidarity with you and your family, but you speak about other things in your statement as well, therefore, I have to ask you about them. So you said that the JNA had come from Novi Sad on the 21st of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that that was the Novi Sad Corps of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So we agree that it didn't come from Novi Sad but that it was, rather, already deployed and that this unit had actually some from Sekovici, which is even deeper inside Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They may have come from Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the names of the remaining places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Did you say other places than Sekovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I said they could have come from Milici, Han Pijesak, or Sekovici, because these are the three roads that lead to Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you do know that these people came from Sekovici; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some elements were billeted at Tildja [as interpreted], near cardboard factory, 1522 garrison was located there, so they may have come from these three directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How big was this unit?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how it -- how big it was. I didn't count. I did see four APCs and tanks. The tanks were near the playing field in Vlasenica, near the stadium. The APCs were at the Muslim graveyard at the exit of Vlasenica. Unfortunately, they drove these APCs around town as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you were in the army. You served; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you recognised or understood or found out that the unit was led by Lieutenant Musa, who is a Yugoslav-Albanian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found that out from a soldier who was born in Bijelo Polje, he is a Montenegrin, he has a specific accent. So when I was talking to him I found out that he was from Bijelo Polje, serving his regular military term of duty in the Novi Sad Corps, and that the commander is a certain Lieutenant Musa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As a man who served in the army, you would know the size of the unit that could be under the command of a lieutenant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that means that it wasn't a large unit; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in view of the number of vehicles, no, it wasn't a large unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statements you say that it was quiet until the 23rd or the 24th of April when the JNA came. However, the JNA came on the 21st of April. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a statement, sir, it says the 21st to the 23rd. So I wasn't precise about the dates of their arrival. They did arrive on the 21st or the 22nd of April, in the early morning. They issued an ultimatum that weapons should be handed over and, that morning, all the local Serbs turned up with standard military weapons, long-barrelled weapons. They had white ribbons around their sleeves, around their arm, so that all sides could tell who was who. People who came from outside didn't know whether I was Ibro, Marko, or Janko. So somebody had to point that out to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your testimony in the Milosevic case, you said that the JNA did not mistreat anyone; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other than asking for the weapons to be handed over, the Yugoslav People's Army did not create any other problems. When the JNA left, all hell broke loose in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We Serbs and Muslims, are we racially different?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, could you please clarify that when you say "racially."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, can you immediately tell who is a Serb and who is a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So how were you able to recognise that there were no Muslims in Musa's unit, other than Musa himself being a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know if there were any Muslims or Serbs in Musa's unit. I met one soldier, and I had contact with that one soldier. With the departure of the JNA from Vlasenica, I know that the only people in Vlasenica who had weapons were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your statement of the 5th to the 7th of October, 1994, you said that you did not see Muslims in Musa's unit, only Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please show that to me so that I can see it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, then we have to call it up in e-court. We have to call up that statement of yours. And while we're looking for that page, would you please tell us: Muslim and Serb soldiers at the time, in the JNA and in the reserve forces, did they wear identical uniforms?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, other than the navy, the whole of the JNA wore identical uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you say that you didn't know if there were any Muslims with weapons and if the Muslims were organised.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Vlasenica, no, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Still -- well, can we please look at ERN 0021876. This is your statement to the bureau for war crimes in Lukavica on the 14th of April, 1993. Page 3 of that statement, ERN 0021876. You said that there was a hodza from Kuglici [phoen] who called the Muslims via loudspeaker to hand over their weapons, and he went to visit the Muslims who did have weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said April 1993. In April 1993, I was in the camp. I was in Batkovic camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we've not got that statement that Dr. Karadzic is asking the question about on the screen, so it's a bit difficult for all of us to follow along. He's now asking about a statement from the 14th of April, 1993, and this isn't it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I can't find that statement in his list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can answer your question, sir. With the occupation of Vlasenica, there was a police vehicle, a Golf, in which Serb policemen put an imam, Hodza Munib Ahmetovic, to call on the Muslim people to hand over their weapons. It's a well-known fact that a large number of people had hunting weapons, both Serbs and Muslims. People had licenses also for pistols. From the vehicle, accompanied by armed persons, Munib called people to hand over their weapons. It's true. I said that and I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Munib called those Muslims for whom he obtained weapons or, rather, those who obtained weapons through the mosque where he served?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that Munib obtained weapons. This is information that the SUP should have and not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see? Is this that statement of yours? It should be third paragraph. Can we scroll up a little bit, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we have the cover page so that the witness is satisfied that this is the document that Dr. Karadzic was referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I apologise. It's not the 4th of April. Actually, the statement was from August, the 4th of August, and not from the 8th of April. I apologise. It's the Lukavac Bureau for War Crimes. This is when you provided this statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am just looking for what you said. I'm trying to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's on page 3, paragraph 3. You state that they were taken to those Muslims who had weapons. This is the third paragraph: "While I was in Vlasenica," it says here, "35 years, there is Munib from Kuglici" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot see where it is in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's Alibegovic, right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Munib Ahmetovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where it says here 35 years, that he was coming by saying it was pointless to put up resistance and that they heard and saw him going to visit with the vehicle those Muslims who had weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says here while I was in Vlasenica during the day --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's ask for the witness to read slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We can't -- I can't find that passage -- Ms. Edgerton, did you find it?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I found it on the original, Your Honour. It's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In English.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: But in the English I don't see it at all, actually, and I wonder perhaps if we can go into the next page on the English just to have a check before we go further. And just -- I can't see even the page reference on the original for us to be able to, for the transcript, identify where it appears in the original. So perhaps we could make that a little bit smaller.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I think I've found it. It's the second penultimate paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: While I was still in Vlasenica." [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "While I was still in Vlasenica, on the first day of the occupation by the Chetniks, I heard from some people that the Vlasenica imam Munib from Kuglici, about 35 years old, appealed to the Muslim people through a loud speaker to surrender their weapons."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can read it. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you were told that they -- that he took them to those Muslims who had weapons; is that correct? This is what you said here.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I said here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know that the hodza could do that because weapons were brought in through the mosque, through the dzemat, and he was distributing them to the resistant movement?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know whether weapons were brought to the mosque. The mosque should not be dealing with the weapons. I don't know if they were distributed through the dzemat, I don't know. I don't know if the hodza distributed the weapons to anyone, but I do know that those people who had weapons had them legally. They had hunting rifles and pistols.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say that the first day of the Serb -- the Chetnik occupation, what is occupation to you, is that from the 21st of April?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the legal, legitimate military force, the JNA, for you are Chetniks and occupiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The legal and the legitimate force which placed itself on the side of one people, if I'm not mistaken, sir, that army should have been on the side of each one of us, on my side and your side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And on ERN 0081-4559 you said that there were only Serbs in Musa's unit, that there were no Muslims there. How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think you asked that question earlier on today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you said after the weapons were handed over the Serbs opened the shops, and you also said that the JNA formed the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at -- just one moment. 65 ter -- well, let's look at 1D3589, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Which wasn't on the Defence list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: But now, on looking at the document, I see it was an associated exhibit by another number. Apologies, I was confused by the lack of reference to the P number or the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that this was written by the Crisis Staff on the 19th of April, 1992, that weapons should be handed over by citizens, not citizens of Muslim ethnicity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this talks about the decision to disarm citizens possessing the firearms illegally, but the vehicles called upon Muslims citizens to hand over their legal and illegal weapons. People of Serb ethnicity walked around in Vlasenica armed with automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're talking about those who had responded to the call-up. Did the Muslims respond to the call-up?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which call-up? There was no call-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know that Izetbegovic declared general mobilisation on the 4th of April?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, because I wasn't a member of the SDA party. So I wasn't really following that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it wasn't a party call-up. It was a state call-up. The Presidency of the B and H, in opposition to the position of the Serbian President, on Bajram, proclaimed a general mobilisation of the TO and the police reserves. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I belonged to the security station for fire-fighting according to the wartime assignment. I was not a member of any military assignment, and police was always part of the MUP or the SUP. I don't know if the call-up was something that applied to them. I do know that I did not receive any call-up summons in Vlasenica from the fire-fighting station, whose member I was for a long number of years. I do know, though, that my neighbours, Serbs in Vlasenica, were armed and that they carried long-barrelled weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please be asked to repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 23115, 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's P3214.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see this document? You were probably shown the document during the proofing, where you can see that before the arrival of the JNA, the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica decided to activate the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica, which up until that time was just proclaimed but was not activated, and that the reason for that was that Muslim deputies and officials had left Vlasenica and there was no formal government.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I do see this piece of paper, and I do see that that Crisis Staff existed. I can see that the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know that a Muslim one should have been formed and there was a signature for that?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, then you're knowledge is not complete, Mr. Osmanovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not really pay attention to the political aspect of the matter. I was born, I lived and worked in that same Vlasenica, and we never divided ourselves into Muslims, and we did not divide up our homes or municipalities, the city, or the village like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we for a moment look at -- oh, no. This is already later in May. All right. So it's not correct that the JNA formed the Serbian municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the Yugoslav People's Army came to Vlasenica, then I saw that the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica was formed. So with the arrival of the JNA, that part, the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica was formed, and the rest of the population, Muslims who were not in the municipality, found out about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But would you agree with me that this was two days before the JNA's arrival?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we look at the dates, that would appear to be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you recall the declaration by the president of the municipality, the joint municipality, which was later to become the Serb municipality? Was that the declaration that you had in mind when you said that there was a declaration that there should be disarmament, that law and order should be re-established and so on?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm just talking about the declaration which talked about disarming, and as for the document itself, in written form, I've never seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you mention Dragisa Milakovic, who was a good friend of yours, and that you were at his place when he received some mail that had to do with mobilisation; correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was at his place when a uniformed man came to his house with call-up papers calling him up to be mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And he was supposed to distribute those call-up papers; correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Those call-up papers for a number of villages, Serb villages in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And he told you on that occasion that you should be careful, that you had no idea who all was carrying weapons in those days, all kinds of idiots; correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you also speak about Milakovic issuing passes for Muslims who wanted to move around the municipality? If any Muslim wanted to walk around a municipality or move about the municipality, Milakovic had to issue them a permit -- a pass, whereas if they wanted it leave Vlasenica permanently, then such a permit would have to be issued by the Crisis Staff of the municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for movement around Vlasenica town and the surrounding lands, because there were some check-points, one at Bregovi and the other at the very approaches to the town, at Novo Naselje, I was on the way --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please answer --

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please let me finish. One of the guards told me that I should report to Dragisa Milakovic in order to be issued a pass if I wanted to move and go from the town to my property, which was there. In other words, from my place to my brother's place, whereas there was an office within the municipality that issued permits for those people who wanted to leave Vlasenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So if Muslims wanted to till their fields and go out of town with -- but remain within the municipality, Milakovic had to issue the passes?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Not -- not just the town but for Vlasenica and the surrounding villages. For instance, my brother lived in Piskavica and I couldn't go to see him without such a permit or pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what you said in your statement. That's 65 ter 00685742, and you said the following: If Muslims wanted to work in the field or go to a town within the territory of the municipality, Milakovic had to issue them a pass. Vlasenica Muslims who wanted to leave the town permanently had to go to the Crisis Staff in order issued a permit to leave the town. You mentioned this only in the context of Muslims. Now, were they conscripts in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can we just go back a minute? There's no such thing as 65 ter 0068-5742, and I just wonder what Dr. Karadzic was referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's ERN. I'm sorry. ERN page 0068574 -- it starts with a 0, and I believe this is page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And what might that be an ERN page of, so that the witness also knows what he might have said?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well that's 740. That's the document we had on the screen a moment ago. We had it just a moment ago. That was the statement that this witness gave in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it to come up, Mr. Osmanovic, tell us, please, did Muslims have to serve in the Serb army and the Serb Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, as far as I know, they were disarmed. Those who did possess weapons legally, I believe that they all had to return their weapons, and none of them served and -- or were conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, please just answer briefly. Were they conscripts and were they considered as such, and were they supposed to also be issued a statement confirming that by the military authorities, or did they just need a permit from the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, only from the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I wonder if we're ever going to get this document 0068-5742, ERN page 0068-5742. That's a statement, but it starts with 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it to come up, Mr. Osmanovic, you mentioned these permits only to refer -- when referring to Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I'm now completely confused. I finally found the ERN number of the document Dr. Karadzic was referring to, and that was the witness's ICTY statement of 10 October 1994, not his statement in Lukavica in 1993. So when Dr. Karadzic told the witness what he had said in that statement in -- that he gave in Lukavica in 1993, I really don't know he was talking about now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you find the passage as well, Ms. Edgerton, in that statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Not so far, but I'm still looking, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 3. So that would be ERN ending with 742. Yes. "On another occasion I wanted to visit," that's how the paragraph begins, "... I wanted to visit my brother in the next town." So we are supposed to find that part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Last paragraph on page 3, continuing to the next page. And whether we are on proper page in B/C/S, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No, we're not. We'll have to go over to the next page so that the witness can see it in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That's on the top of the page. The first sentence at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "If Muslims wanted to work in the field or go to a town within the municipality, Milakovic had to grant permission. Muslims in Vlasenica who wanted to permanently leave the town had to go to the Crisis Committee to get permission to leave Vlasenica." Correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's what it says, but in Vlasenica there's only one town. All the other settlements are just villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but did you say this?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now get 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the accused please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 23218, 65 ter 23218. 53218; correct? Yes. 53218. Yes. Now we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this. Sir, would you take a look, Mr. Osmanovic, at this document to see how the permits for leaving town were issued by the competent authorities. If they are leaving town permanently, they had to issue a statement saying that it was voluntary. So if we look at item 3, it says: "To be allowed to travel to other areas, conscripts of Serbian nationality must have a permit from the municipal TO staff showing that their leave has been granted." And then it goes on to discuss the check-points. And then paragraph 4 -- actually, we see it twice, so it's probably paragraph 5: "Special attention is to be paid to individuals and armed persons from other areas who want to enter the town. All individuals are to be asked to show their licence to carry weapons and information on who they are being sent to is to be checked. "This particularly applies to individuals who have a history of thieving or other deviant behaviour, often concealing themselves behind their uniform."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: This is P3218 referred to in the witness's amalgamated statement at paragraph 58. So Dr. Karadzic is reading in a document that the witness has previously seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, can you see that this actually applies to all citizens with the exception of Serb conscripts? In other words, the Muslims were not -- they didn't have to bring anything from the military office, but the Serbs did.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what it says there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But would you agree, Mr. Osmanovic, that in wartime or an emergency it was necessary to -- it is necessary to control the movement of individuals, especially conscripts, in order to make sure that they weren't deserters, that they didn't have any background agendas of their own and so on?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can only speak about the municipality of Vlasenica. Everyone knew everyone. We knew what meals people had on any given day, as it were. You are correct. It had to be checked, the streets and so on. The situation had to be checked in wartime conditions, but at the time, I could no longer see people of different ethnicities. At the time, there was no police anymore, there were no municipal organs or municipal government. Everything had a moniker added to it, Serbian, so --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his last word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreters couldn't hear your last word, Mr. Osmanovic. What is reflected in the transcript is: "Everything had a moniker added to it, Serbian," and then it's missing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, because everything was Serbian, the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica, the Serb autonomous district. There was no joint police anymore, no joint security organs. Only one ethnicity was armed and that one ethnicity could move around. There was a curfew, so that all the others were no longer welcome in that town, although we were local. We were born there. Unfortunately, that's how it remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Osmanovic, in order to draw that kind of conclusion, you have to look at the whole picture, not just part of it. Now, do you know that the Muslims agreed to have their own municipality, whether they would call it the Muslim municipality or Vlasenica, Bosniak municipality, whatever, that's what was agreed, and that Muslims actually fled Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please take a look at 1D4127.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, you said a moment ago that you didn't see that there was a threat of war --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Also not on the Defence list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You overlapped, Ms. Edgerton. Could you repeat, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: 1D4127 is not on the Defence list either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then let us hear whether it's also part of Prosecution associate -- no. Mr. Karadzic, you're talking about disclosure violation and then you are using a lot of unnoticed documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I received this document very late, and as for the statement, the amalgamated statement, of Mr. Osmanovic was in such a format that I could not access it on my computer, and also I received all the documents that were disclosed to me at the very last moment. And just to add another thing, this is the same document that I asked for earlier. It's that same document. So it's not a new document. Can we now see a bulletin of the Serb news agency. That's what we have before us. Can we see the fourth page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, I don't follow when Mr. Karadzic said this is the document he asked for earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've already mentioned this document earlier today, but it hadn't been uploaded. It's the same document that I asked for at the very beginning of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, the amalgamated statement was transmitted to Dr. Karadzic electronically in the same format these statements are always provided to him. The documents referred to by the witness in the amalgamated statement were cited in the draft statement that was forwarded on the 12th of August. I can't see how he can justifiably explain some last-minute disclosure in this regard and as a justification for using an unnoticed document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you're objecting to using this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes. This time, yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber will allow you to continue, but in the future, please make sure that you give proper notice to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We shall equally be tolerant to the opposing side, but please believe we are really suffering under the load of our burden.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the interpreters couldn't hear your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked the witness whether it was true that Rabija was a Muslim name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And I can also add: Did you now that Rabija Subic was a modern Muslim woman, as probably you yourself were -- and she was the president of the Socialist Party of BH?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that Rabija Subic is a Muslim name. However, whether she was a modern-oriented person, whether she was the president of that particular party, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at this public announcement coming from her party and in the first section she says what she holds Mr. Izetbegovic responsible for. But please focus on the last paragraph, where it says: "We warn you about blood shedding and final tragedy of the so-called independence of the BH, Mr. Izetbegovic, and we invite you to act upon an example of Vlasenica and Bratunac where agreements between Muslims and Serbs were made without a single bullet shot, without violence, crime, and without terror." And look at the top where it says out of these bullet numbers. She's asking him whether he was aware that there was a Catholic-Germanic conspiracy to sacrifice the Muslims in the Balkans. Can you see, therefore, that there was an agreement that you know nothing about?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, if I look at this paper produced by the Serbian news agency SRNA, this is what it says, and it says, "We warn you about the ultimate tragedy and blood shedding," and then it goes on to cite the examples of Vlasenica and Bratunac. Vlasenica exactly went through this bloody experience without a single bullet shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, let us make this very accurate. This was not written by the Serbian news agency, it was only published by it, but it was written by the Socialist Party of BH. Secondly, it was written before Vlasenica went through this bloody time, and it just says that it was possible to avoid this bloody outcome by citing these examples.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton. Probably the Chamber does not need your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't think, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see any basis to admit this.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I was looking to see if the witness had even at a stretch confirmed something but I can't find it. Your Honours may find -- and in all fairness I was looking to see if there might be some contextual assistance, but I -- I don't take a position, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will not admit this, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, my position is that this is a significant document which demonstrates that the witness knows only half the truth and that if he had given statement knowing the full truth would have been -- it would have been different. The Serbian municipality of Vlasenica is not what -- all what it comes to. It was something that was subject to an agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber gave its ruling. If you'd like to tender that document, please call another witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that the JNA had left their equipment behind. Do you know that Colonel Tacic took a rocket brigade away, something that I will never forgive him. He took it from Mount Romanija in spite of all the opposition from the Serbian side. The Serbs, the Muslims, and the Croats equally put a ban on taking any equipment away.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who Colonel Tacic was and where he took this rocket unit. I do know, though, that in Vlasenica the weapons remained that had been in the position of the JNA, that every single Serb in Vlasenica was armed overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Didn't you yourself name a Muslim village that was also armed, but it was loyal to Yugoslavia as a state? And I'm talking about Brezevo Polje.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Esteemed sir, Brezevo Polje is 150 kilometres away. It's on the River Sava near Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not denying that, but do you agree that you said that you knew that they had weapons, that they were Muslims who were loyal and who took part in fighting against the Croats?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard at Batkovic that they were guarding their village from the Croats and I heard it from those very same people that the Serbs brought later to Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Osmanovic, nobody disarmed the people of Brezevo Polje for as long as they were loyal to the common state, and they had been given weapons by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who armed them. According to the stories I heard from people from Brezevo Polje at Batkovic camp was that they were regarding the embankment on the Sava to prevent incursions from Croatia. Allegedly, all of them were later brought to Batkovici. Some were released sooner, some later, but the whole group from Brezevo Polje was brought to Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, I don't have time to go into details. Now let's clarify this: You say that in May 1992, the Muslims were restricted in withdrawing money to the amount between 5.000 and 10.000 dinars?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that a Yugoslavia dinar still at the time?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that it was made in the -- that it was printed in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the central bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the payments of both dinar and for X amount had been introduced back in 1989 by Ante Markovic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the dinars. I know about the foreign exchange though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that it was necessary to transport the printed money, the dinars, to Vlasenica during war?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I was not involved in any transportation of money. I didn't work for a bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, sir, the shortage of cash had nothing to do with religion. This lack was called -- caused by the fact because it -- the money was printed in a foreign country and there was a border installed.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the money was short, then it was short for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Therefore, as of the 6th of April, when war broke out in Bosnia-Herzegovina, up until the 22 May, you didn't face any problems; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, except for the curfew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us whether you were arrested on the 22nd of May?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you arrested at home or some place else?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was brought to the police station for the first time when I tried to withdraw money, and the second time I was arrested on the 22nd of May at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when was the first time?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you say that you were detained in a solitary confinement for six days; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, in another statement you say that you were released and that you were requested to report to them on a daily basis and that you were arrested again on the 28th of May. Which of these -- this information is correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Show me the paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, for example, in your statement -- just a moment. In your statement given on the 8th of March, 2010, that's IT-08-91 case --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please slowly read the numbers. We are really struggling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, slow down when you read out some numbers or passages from the statement. Could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the case number is IT-08-91-T, and page is 7303. It was an examination conducted on the 8th of March, 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On that occasion you said that they came to your house to arrest you and that you were taken to a room where there were another 20 Muslims.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I look at this document in an electronic form?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, let it be called up. This is a court document. It's case number IT-08-91-T. It's a trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we do not have every document in our e-court. What's the -- what's the e-court -- 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With Court indulgence, we managed to identify --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I think Dr. Karadzic is referring to Mr. Osmanovic's testimony in the Stanisic and Zupljanin proceedings, and that's 65 ter 2227A.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The letter A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's a different thing. Page number, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 7303. This is 7299. We have to go five pages ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here: "[In English] At the station I was put in a room where there were other 20 Muslim men." [Interpretation] And then you go on to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us find the passage first.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says: "[In English] ... and Zoran came to my house to arrest me. At the station I was put in the room where there were other 20 Muslim men." [Interpretation] Once we locate the names, the problem will be solved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is a part of question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: No. No. The answer was: "Bastah Rade and Zoran came to my house to arrest me." [Interpretation] Can we look briefly at the statement given between the 5th and 7th October 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this. "[In English] In your written statement, you stated --" Can we have the previous, please. No. Which was prior to the last change. Okay. Okay. Okay. "In your testimony, in your written statement, you state that the police arrested you, brought you to the SJB building and placed you in a gaol cell along with up to 20 other Muslim men." [Interpretation] So how do you say that you were confined in solitary confinement?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a solitary confinement. It was renovated into like a gaol. We were standing like sardines, the 20 of us. This was in the Vlasenica police station. The first floor, we were in a room that was turned into a cell from a toilet, and the second floor, it was turned from a weapons storage room into a cell.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat the question and the witness the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. You are overlapping so quickly the interpreters have -- are struggling to follow you. Mr. Karadzic, the -- before you repeat the question, how much longer do you have for this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I need a whole session. My hands are tied, really. I cannot allow so many inconsistencies, incorrect things, and untruths to pass. So I kindly ask to be given enough time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for 20 minutes and resume at 20 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you continue, Mr. Karadzic, Judge Baird has a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: During the course of your evidence earlier this morning, Dr. Karadzic asked you: "Did you know the SDA was arming the Muslims and that the Patriotic League in every municipality already had their staff and unit?" And your answer was: "I don't know that it existed in Vlasenica." Do you recollect that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Now, the question carried two components. The first component: Did you know the SDA was arming the Muslims? Can you give us your answer to that component?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the SDA party, I was not a member of the party. I wasn't, and none of my family was, so I don't know if the party armed anyone or not. But with the hand-over of the weapons in Vlasenica, they said that there was a certain number of firearms, Kalashnikovs, with people who were members of the SDA party. This is something that I saw on television. This was shown by Television Novi Sad. They showed footage taped in the police station in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed. Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, as I emphasised several times before, the Chamber has -- has been carefully considering the amount of time that is appropriate for your cross-examination of the witnesses, and in this case two hours is, in the Chamber's view, more than sufficient. I find it quite inappropriate for you to raise this issue continuously while you keep spending time exploring irrelevant or marginally relevant issues. You will have 40 minutes to conclude this, your cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, were you arrested the way you describe in your statement of the 27th of July, 1993, or were you arrested in a different manner?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please show me where I said that I was arrested on the 27th of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you were taken to solitary confinement where you were alone.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was alone in that room in the beginning. Then they took me to another room where there was about 20 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How long were you alone?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly how long I was alone. If you have written proof, could you please show it to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you arrested at home or were you arrested on the street?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was brought in for the first time from in front of the bank and the second time I was arrested at my house, and I never returned to my house again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When was it you were arrested in front of the bank?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember when I was detained at the bank. I tried to withdraw a certain amount of money but Stevo Mumovic picked me up from in front of the bank and took me away. The second time, I was taken away by Bastah from my family house, to which, to my regret, I never, ever returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What were you suspected of?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked where the gun or the cannon was. They asked me who had weapons, whom -- to whom had the party issues weapons. Well, since a cannon is not a needle that you can hide somewhere or put it in your pocket, and in view of the fact that I was not a member of the party, I really wasn't able to answer. Dragisa Milakovic confirm the information that I was his acquaintance, I was not a member of the party, and that I was not a person who was armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then were you released or were you held for these six days like it says in the statement?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please show me the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. "[In English] Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, 2nd Corps command, SP number 10/101-114-6/93." [Interpretation] Of the 28th of July, 1993, you said there that you spent six days alone in detention. "Nobody mistreated us, but I did not get any food for those six days, and then Boro Mijic came and brought us kebabs." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that Boro Mijic brought kebabs, but I would like to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, I don't have time. You gave four statements and you testified four times plus you gave statements to the Muslim authorities. How am I supposed to have time to go through every inconsistency and incorrect thing that you have said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's quite an improper statement. If the witness wants to see his statement, you have to -- you're obliged to show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all right. Can we have 1D04119 then, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is your statement of the 27th of July, 1993. On the first page do you see: "On the 22nd of May, at about 0800 hours, policeman Bastah took me out of my house." And then on the 28th of May, this guy came in and brought you kebabs and yogurt; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true that that is what it states.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, in a different place you say something else. This is your statement. Just one moment. This is the District Court Tuzla. No, this is the State Security Service. Just a minute. On the 27th of July, 1993, you stated at the Lukavica Municipal Court -- no, no. On the 4th of August, 1993. 4th of August, 1993. I apologise. It's page 0190-8934. You said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it is a statement of 27th of July, this must be it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the SUP, and this is the court of the 4th of August, 4th of August. We had that a little bit earlier as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you state there that on the 22nd of May, the three of you were picked up from the street, and you were interrogated at the police station by Ljuban Stanisic, each one of us was slapped once or twice, and then you were freed on condition that you report every 24 hours back to them. So what is correct here?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was arrested and detained on the 22nd of May. Probably there's a mistake here, sir, as far as the dates are concerned. And it's not the Lukavica court, because I never gave a statement for the Lukavica court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The bureau for war crimes.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not a court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. So were you released on condition that you are to report back every 24 hours?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was brought in, the first day I was released and told to report on my way back or to work. I was questioned by Ljuban Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. On the 28th of May you say that you were arrested by Dragan Bastah at your house. So from the 22nd of May until the 28th of May, were you conditionally released?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm just saying now that this is a mistake in the dates. I was taken away from my family home by Dragan Bastah, aka Czar. Somebody called him Dragan, som people called him Predrag, but everybody called him Czar. I was conditionally released.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that you were arrested on the 22nd of May, that you were confined to solitary for six days and that -- once you said that you were arrested on the street and the second time you said that you were arrested at home. And then from the answer that you were conditionally released, this was not in the transcript, and I really have a problem with time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me Excellencies, but with so many statements from this witness I must have problems with time, because I have to show everything the witness is not consistent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You could have started your cross-examination with this question. You spent -- wasted a lot of time in the previous session. Please get on with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first time you were brought in was on the 22nd of May.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I was brought in from in front of the bank. The second time I was taken in from my house. There is a mistake in the dates.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic repeat his question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were conditionally released after -- actually, you were released on condition that you report in after you were asked about the cannon and other weapons.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you think that the fact that they had confiscated a Kalashnikov from a friend of yours from a check-point could have made you suspicious as well?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I wasn't armed. I wasn't a member of the party. I could not have been in possession of a cannon, so I don't see any reason why that would be so. However, everybody was suspicious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you say that perhaps they suspected you because your friend at a check-point had a Kalashnikov confiscated from him?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mensur Smajic handed in a rifle. He was a colleague of mine. He told me that. I didn't know that he had the weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So he did not hand it over, but it was found on him at the check-point.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if he handed it in or if it was confiscated at the check-point. I was asked if I knew where Mensur Smajic got a gun from because they said that we socialised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So was that the basis for you being brought in; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't say that that was the only basis for my being brought in, because they were looking for some kind of cannon. They were asking who was arming people, who was distributing weapons, who was selling weapons. Since I was not involved with that and I never had anything like that, any need for that in my life, I was not able to answer any of those questions. But they could have found a thousand reasons to bring me in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But they didn't ask you about a thousand reasons but they specifically asked you about the gun and the piece of weapon found on your friend.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They also asked me about the street guard since Dragan Milakovic had confirmed that I had never been either a member of the party or armed, and I didn't even participate in those guards. I was most of the time in his company. That is what saved my skin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that back at the time where there was joint police and joint patrols, the Muslims had their own check-points on the way to Drum village, and they had their own guards?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Drum is populated by the Muslims alone with the exception of two Serb houses. It is true that there was a check-point manned by the Muslims, but whether they were armed or not, I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that in Zaklopaca, grenades with incendiary phosphorous were used, which as you well know did not exist in the JNA arsenal.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Incendiary weapons do exist, and it existed in the arsenal of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You spoke about phosphorous grenades. Did the JNA have these kind of grenades?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please show me where I said that it was a phosphorous grenade? I only said that it was incendiary ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you never mentioned white phosphorous?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have offered an explanation as to what it might have been, but I would like to see that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you mentioned the white phosphorous only as part of your explanation of what it might have been but not of what it was?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see my statement. I don't want to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that no houses or anything were burnt in Zaklopaca?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four houses on the entry point of Zaklopaca were burnt, and all the population was annihilated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And those four houses were facing the separation line; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no separation line there. When you go from Zaklopaca towards Milici, you come across the Serbian village of Podgora, the village of Bojanic is above Zaklopaca, then Gornji Zalukovik, then there is Tabana on the other side, another Serb village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement given 5 to 7 October, 1994, that before the JNA had come to Vlasenica, at the crossroads between the road and pavement, I -- you said that you thought that at the beginning the village of Drum was better armed.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said, and I stand by it. I said that of the whole population, only young people remained. Unfortunately, that did not apply to Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please do not expand your answers to cover other items, because that will take much more time. Can we now look at page 0018-4561, where you speak about white phosphorous. So 0018-4561, page 4557. The date is the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4557. That's not the statement we need.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, yes, it is. That's his statement of 10 October 1994, to the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 00619. And the Serbian page is 0018 -- actually, this is an English page, 0018-4561.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you see in the English version where you speak about Zaklopaca and the phosphorous grenades?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it in the B/C/S version, and I said here when the JNA came --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, for my colleagues in the booth, could Mr. Osmanovic slow down a little bit as he reads, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Let us find the passage first.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version, it's the full paragraph in the middle of the page on the left-hand side, and it's the second full paragraph in the middle of the page on the right-hand side, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's what you heard. You don't know about this. You only heard of it, and you incorporated that into your statement.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, as for these ribbons, Mr. Osmanovic, why should one put a ribbon around their sleeves?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the local Serbs of Vlasenica wore those white ribbons as a sign of recognition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
