utterances.text: Uh-huh, so it means there were another army wearing the same uniforms and the only way to distinguish between the two was based on those ribbons?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because nobody else was either uniformed or armed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go briefly into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 18th of June, I was transferred from the municipal prison to Susica camp, and then on the 30th of June, I was transferred from Susica to Batkovic camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your statements you mention this hodza as well as other Muslims and you label them as traitors.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please let us be specific. In what way did I label this hodza and other Muslims as traitors? I did say that hodza called upon people via a megaphone to surrender their weapons, but where did I say that he was a traitor, among other things?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you think that what you said about hodza was a positive thing, that it was all right for him to say that any resistance would be futile?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was forced to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, that's too fast. Too fast. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't have any remote reference about where this whole line of questioning has been drawn from, and I think it would be of assistance to be directed to any comments by the witness in previous statements or testimonies regarding the hodza. It's a whole line of questioning. We don't know where it comes from, yet Dr. Karadzic says it comes from his previous statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We demonstrated that he mentioned hodza in his statement, and I'm asking the witness whether it was something positive about hodza or was he implicitly criticising him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I wasn't criticising. I just think that he was forced to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in Batkovic, at least three Muslims were enjoying a sort of privileged position that were in charge of taking prisoners to perform labour and sometimes went out to carry out looting?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What's the name -- what is the name of those people?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slowly tell us the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, please pause before you start answering the question, and the interpreters this time could not hear your answer, in particular the names of these people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. There were three of them, Dzemal Zahirovic, aka Spajzer, and Django, a Roma from Zenica. Then Bekric Esad, aka Policeman, and the third one was Fikret of Brezevo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So it seems, according to you, that Smajlovic was appointed as a guard or a chief in another building?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's how he behaved, as a person in charge. He was the only one among the prisoners who had his private car. He was the only person who went in and out of the camp whenever he pleased. And that was Smajlovic of Brezevo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in another statement you said that he slept in the same building and elsewhere you say that he slept in a separate building.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning, he had different sleeping quarters from the other detainees. He was the only one who had a collapsible bed on which he slept. He was the only one who had unlimited access to everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that Zahirovic led groups into the fields to perform work?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is true that Zahirovic led the groups initially to work the fields and then later to Koraj to plunder the Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To plunder the Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To plunder of Muslim village Koraj. Trucks, tractors, other machinery were driven away. Furniture was collected. Everything was done in the same way in Svinjari and other villages, and the houses were left empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And he took other prisoners with him?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were escorted by armed guards. He was the one who designated who was going to be in the group and he acted as the group leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is Zahirovic a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is. He's a Roma of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These Muslims from Vlasenica and other places who enjoyed different treatment believed that you who did not enjoy this treatment -- blamed you for the conflict with the Serbs and did they resent that?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who were together with me experienced the same things as I did. There was no need for us to be angry at one another. All we needed was to survive and get out of there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Whenever you went to perform labour, you very precisely noted in your statement of 27th June 1993, in Tuzla, as to the exact deployment of the Serbian troops and weapons.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the sector of Majevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have to skip things in order to stick to the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have five minutes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your statements you said that after the events in Bijeljina where you say it was declared that Arkan had come to prevent conflicts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then after Zvornik there were refugees going to Kladanj, Muslim refugees going to Kladanj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And were there Serb refugees coming from Kladanj going to Sekovici and Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Sekovici, but I know that in the secondary school in Vlasenica, when we were brought back from prison I saw a number of Serb ethnic -- ethnic Serb refugees who were billeted at the school. I didn't see them when I left there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in your statement of 8th of August or actually the 4th of August, 1993, 1D04121, stated that in March until May, the Muslims from the Vlasenica municipality held meetings which you attended and at which it was concluded that you would need to be in a state of readiness?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct that I did attend one such meeting. It was in my neighbourhood. No one was armed, but we were told to be in a state of readiness with others. I emphasise "with others," because other groups were preparing to come to Vlasenica. Local Serbs were never mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you state that you knew that earlier weapons were shipped in and that it was supposed to be distributed to the Muslims in the same statement?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear about a shipment of weapons. I don't know who these weapons were distributed to, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the first page of that statement you said that in late February, the weapons with secretly brought in on two occasions to Vlasenica, in Zastava trucks, intended for Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, but I have the statement of the 4th of August, 1993, in front of me, and I can't find anything that bears any resemblance to any of the questions that Dr. Karadzic asserts the witness said in that statement. I wonder if he needs to double-check the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I hope he can come back to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 8th of August. The 8th of August. The 8th of August, and we have that now in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, but this here at the top is not my name or my surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I apologise. But you were at the same meeting with this man?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not my name or my surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you were at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did attend one meeting. I did say that. But this is not my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. And is it correct that in Mustafa Zildzic's garage weapons were transported with a PZ car?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mustafa Zildzic's garage?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is not my statement. Can you please give me my statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the security organ of the 2nd Corps, did you say to them that you were not mistreated by anyone?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not mistreated by anyone when I was at home. I said that the last time you asked me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And for the six days when you were in prison, from the 22nd of May, that nobody mistreated you. Pages 5, 6, and that is 1D04122. Do you recall giving this statement?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just let me take a look for a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It states on page 1 that nobody mistreated you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that nobody mistreated me at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you read it -- why don't you read the remainder of that sentence?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot find it, Your Excellency. I have to rush.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody maltreated me for six days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: "Nobody maltreated me, but I was given no food for six days."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. And now I'm asking him about -- about -- about physical mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the first day that I was brought in there was no physical mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, now it's time for you to come to your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you said that you recognise that most of the policemen who were dealing with the prisoners were from the reserve forces and were not professional policemen?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not part of the professional work-force earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Ms. Edgerton, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just one if I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, today at pages 30 and -- 30 to 31, lines 25 of page 30, over 4 of page 31, Dr. Karadzic and you were talking about shortage of cash in Vlasenica, and Dr. Karadzic said that: "The shortage of cash had nothing to do with religion. This lack was caused by the fact that the money was printed in a foreign country and there was a border installed." And your answer was: "If the money was short, then it was short for everyone." And do you remember that question and answer?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Was the money, in fact, short for everyone?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that, Madam Prosecutor. I wouldn't say that the money was short for everybody. I watched my Serb neighbours withdraw unlimited quantities of money. They could withdraw unlimited quantities both in the form of checks or cash, but it was limited as far as I was concerned. I was subject to limitations, as well as my colleagues of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I -- may I just ask the witness to be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who received more money? We're going to obtain bank records which would indicate that it was limited for everybody.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People of Serb ethnicity --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Name?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm just saying it was limited for Serb -- ethnic Serbs. But you can obtain the records, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, I'm sorry, there -- I wonder if we could just go back to the last sentence in Dr. Karadzic's redirect. The witness is said to have said, "Well, I'm just saying it was limited for ethnic Serbs," and I just --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It wasn't limited for ethnic Serbs but it was limited for everyone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you to my colleagues for the correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, just -- yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence has a need to test the assertions of the witness. If it is a neighbour, then that neighbour has a name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You put the question and the witness has answered the question. Mr. Osmanovic, that concludes your evidence. The Chamber would like to express its gratitude to you for coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go. Have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I address the Chamber before the next witness comes in, in public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will take a few minutes. I would kindly ask for your patience. I would like to say that this coming witness gave a number of interviews and statements to the OTP which are quite inconsistent, and in line with the other evidence and also with exhibits. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President. Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's improper. We go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We go into open session. Yes. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. What I would like to say is that over 95 per cent of witnesses are testifying pursuant to 92 ter or 92 bis. There are very few live witnesses. With witnesses who provided a number of statements and testified a number of times, amalgamated statements are a creation of the Prosecution. They're very selective and present only matters that suit the OTP. In our system, this could not happen, because the investigative judge would insist on objectivity and would obtain elements important for both sides. I understand that the adversarial system is different. We're not used to such a system, but if we are affected by that system, which is foreign and unusual to us, then we must not forget the right to equality of arms. But there can be no equality of arms if I have so little time and ability to prepare to rebut statements and documents that accompany the testimony of such witnesses and if I'm not given time to finish that job completely. That is why I believe that it is a question -- all these questions, 92 bis, where the witness don't come, 92 ter, where the witnesses are there to very ambitiously retell the indictment and the indictment is offered up as proof accompanied by a protected witness, all of that, I'm afraid, is something that is creating a precedent, which would be something very unfavourable for future proceedings or the jurisprudence would in theory very soon be condemned because of the way these proceedings are conducted pursuant to these rules are prejudicial absolutely to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, again you always go back to that issue all the time. Again I emphasise the Chamber carefully considers all the -- all the factors in deciding the proper amount of time that is appropriate for your cross-examination of the witnesses. As I explained to you earlier on, you don't have to explore every single issue with every witness. The Chamber is aware of the fact that you are a self-represented accused who is not a lawyer. For that reason, we give you a certain latitude both when assessing the amount of time to be given for your cross-examination and when assessing how your cross-examination is going. However, you cannot continue to make unreasonable demands. You have to take some responsibility for the fact that you have chosen to represent yourself, which carries with it certain burdens and implications. As to the efficient way to conduct your cross-examination, please consult your legal advisors. For the next witness we go into -- we'll hear the evidence in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. President. And --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just add something, Excellency?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not this time, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We'll some need time both for the Registrar's preparation and also to make the transition for the computers here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I need to hear the confirmation from the Registry that the maximum amount of time we can go in one go is hundred minutes, 1 hour and 40 minutes in terms of tape.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You didn't answer, Excellency, to my request for the witness to testify viva voce. That would only be the third such witness. The third, only the third witness that would testify live.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, at this moment I don't see any reason we would reconsider our decision to hear the witness pursuant to Rule 92 ter. As in the previous cases, things may change depending upon the answers given by the witness when he was asked about his previous statement, but that is something we have to see. At this moment, the Chamber is not minded to change our previous attitude. We'll have a break, take a break for half an hour, and resume at quarter past, and I think we can go to the end of today's session from there on. Quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 31st day of August, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
